# =============================================================================
# semgrep-excluded-rules.txt — repo-wide semgrep rule suppressions
# =============================================================================
#
# Consumed by .github/scripts/run-semgrep.sh, which turns each non-comment,
# non-blank line into a `--exclude-rule <id>` flag for `semgrep scan`. Keeping
# the suppressed rule IDs in this version-controlled data file (mirroring
# .github/config/.trivyignore and .github/config/.pip-audit-ignore) means a
# suppression is reviewed as an explicit data change rather than being buried
# inside pipeline YAML, and every caller shares this one list.
#
# Format: one full semgrep rule ID per line. Inline comments (from `#`) and
# blank lines are ignored. Prefer fixing a finding over suppressing it; only add
# a rule here when the finding is a deliberate, documented project choice.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The list is intentionally empty.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# It previously held `github-actions-mutable-action-tag`, which flags
# `uses: owner/action@<tag>` because a tag is a mutable pointer the action's
# publisher can move onto different code. That suppression is gone because the
# finding is gone: every third-party action is now pinned to a 40-character
# commit SHA with the tag kept as a trailing `# vX.Y.Z` comment, so Dependabot
# still recognizes and bumps it while the ref itself cannot be repointed.
# `tests/test_workflow_security_contract.py` fails the build if a tag ref or a
# comment-less SHA comes back, so re-adding this rule here would hide a
# regression that CI already refuses to merge.
#
# Keep the file even while empty: run-semgrep.sh degrades to "no excludes" if it
# is missing, and an empty-but-present list is the reviewable place a future
# suppression goes.
